stages.line: Imagine the school wants to display the names of students.

stages.title: What *information* is this?
stages.line: Can a program understand names too?
stages.right: These are names written as text.
stages.wrong: Look at the names. Are they numbers?

stages.line: Which of these can be treated as text?

props.hint: Text can hold letters, digits and symbols.

children: A value is not a number just because it has digits. A phone number or a student ID identifies someone: we don’t add or subtract it.

finishPanel.title: All of them!
finishPanel.text: Text holds letters, numbers and symbols.

stages.line: Text information is called a String.

stages.line: Look at these two values: 12 and “12”.

stages.right: A value’s look doesn’t always show its type.
stages.wrong: Joining text puts the characters side by side.

stages.line: What kind of information is the teacher collecting?
stages.right: It tells us whether something is true or false.
stages.wrong: Present or absent: how many answers?

stages.right: Each situation has two possible logical states.
stages.wrong: Look at the two states each picture can show.

stages.line: Information with two values is a Boolean.

children: Boolean (bool) represents a logical value: True or False.
